blocks.text:
I need to find the most severe steric clash between residue pairs. I'm considering whether the zinc ion coordinated by cysteine sulfurs counts, but the question is likely about amino acid residue pairs, so I'm checking distances like Cys135's SG atom relative to the zinc center.

Zinc's bonds to Cys135 and Cys128 look normal, so I'm turning to search for actual non-bonded clashes near the chain breaks in the sequence, and checking various cysteine SG-SG pairs to see if any potential disulfides are unusually close or far. None of the obvious candidates (Cys130/Cys184, Cys256/Cys282, Cys184/Cys282) seem to be clashing, so I'll need to compute pairwise distances more systematically across the structure to find the actual severe clash.

With 1160 atoms, manual pairwise checking isn't feasible exhaustively, so I'm trying to narrow down by scanning spatial clusters and side chain tips that might overlap, particularly around Met149, Met145, His152, and other bulky residues with long flexible chains that could plausibly intersect with neighboring backbone atoms.

I'm grouping atoms by x-coordinate bins to narrow down spatial neighbors, listing out Pro125, Tyr126, Ser140, Leu141, Asp142, Ala143, Thr214, Arg215, Lys216, Gln217, and His244 side chain positions to compare against each other for proximity, checking Pro125 against Ser140 and finding their z-coordinates are too far apart to be relevant.

Now I'm checking distances between Asp142's acidic side chain and Lys216's basic side chain, but the y-coordinates diverge too much for a salt bridge contact. I also compare Ser140's hydroxyl to Asp142's beta carbon, and His244's ring atoms to Tyr126's ring atoms, but none of these pairs come close enough. I'm scanning Arg215's guanidinium group against nearby residues like Glu219, but the z-coordinates rule those out too, so I'm shifting strategy to look specifically at backbone atoms that might be in close contact, possibly near the zinc-coordinating cysteines.

I'm now cross-checking the coordinates for Asn171, Ile170, and their neighboring atoms, trying to verify whether I misread a sign on the x-coordinate in the original structure file, since some values look like they might have flipped between positive and negative.

Given the structure spans a wide x-range, I realize manually scanning every atom pair for clashes is impractical, so I'm considering whether this clash might mirror a known real-world PDB structural conflict, like a common Arg side-chain collision.

I try tracing the zinc coordination sphere, checking which Cys and His residues fall within bonding distance of the Zn atom, tentatively identifying Cys128, Cys135, and His147 as likely ligands while ruling out others that are too far. With the metal site mapped out, I shift to systematically grouping atoms by z-coordinate to narrow down candidate clash pairs.

I consider using a coarse spatial hash to bin atoms into 4 Å cells so I can check nearby residues for overlapping side chains more efficiently, since scanning every pair by hand is too slow. I check a few isolated candidates like Lys153 and Lys136 but they seem too exposed to be involved, so I start listing residue centroids to narrow down which interior pairs are worth checking closely for a sub-2.2 Å clash.

Still computing trajectory positions...

Now that I have all the CA coordinates, I'm scanning for residue pairs that are spatially close but far apart in sequence, then checking their actual side-chain atom distances. I've checked a few candidates like residues 190/210 and 191/209 so far, finding distances in the 4-5 range but not close enough to flag as clashes.

This exhaustive pairwise search is too slow, so I'm trying to bucket the CA coordinates into spatial bins by dividing each residue's position into rough 6 Å cells, which should let me focus only on residues sharing nearby bins instead of comparing every pair.

I'm checking residue pairs within this z-range cluster for close side-chain contacts, comparing atom coordinates like His147 and Gln151, then moving on to Pro125 versus Gly139 to see if their distances are close enough to flag as a potential interaction.

Now I'm scanning cluster B (residues 169-178) and cluster C (residues 194-261) for similar proximity checks, comparing side-chain atom positions like Lys195's CE/NZ and Gln204's CB to rule out contacts, then continuing to residues 196, 203, 248, and 251 to look for pairs within bonding distance.

I'm also grouping residues by a narrower z-range (-6 to -1) to spot another potential cluster spanning residues 141-272, then checking x/y coordinates within that slab to see if 141-149 form a distinct spatial group separate from 244.

Checking distances within the x -5..3, y -10..-16 subgroup, none of these residue pairs (148/152, 149/153, 152/155) come close enough to be meaningful contacts given their side-chain atom positions. Now I'm scanning the x 1..8, y -1..-6 slab covering residues 178, 179, 192, 193, and 177 for similar distance checks.

Moving to a new z-slab spanning roughly -1 to 4, I list residues with coordinates in that range and start checking candidate pairs for proximity, focusing first on Phe189 versus Leu211, where I'm measuring the distance between Phe189's aromatic ring atoms and Leu211's branched side chain to see if any atoms fall within contact range.

I'm now scanning other nearby pairs — Pro240/Gln210, Arg241/Gln210, Arg241/Ala250 — comparing their side-chain atom coordinates to check for close contacts, and moving on to look at residues 266, 268, and 272 in a different region of the structure.

I'm then grouping residues by z-coordinate range (roughly 4 to 9) and systematically checking distances between residue pairs like 187/217, 188/239, 223/237, 225/235, 226/234, and 227/234, looking at both CA distances and specific side-chain atom positions to see if any are close enough to matter.

Moving to residues with z above 9, I'm listing out candidates (159-163, 184-186, 220-233, 278-282) and starting to check pairwise distances among them for potential contacts.

Checking Asp162 and Thr278 more closely, I find their side chains sit near each other with OD1 and OG1 roughly 2.68 apart, which reads as a reasonable hydrogen bond rather than a steric clash. I continue scanning down the list, comparing residues 184 and 185 against 280 and 281 for similar proximity.

Still not finding an obvious clash in these pairwise checks, I widen my search to long side chains that could reach farther than CA-CA distances suggest -- Arg, Lys, Gln, Glu, Met, Trp, Tyr, Phe, His. I check Lys136's NZ tip, Lys153's NZ, and Lys195's NZ against nearby atoms, but each of these lysine tips appears solvent-exposed with nothing close enough to cause a steric problem, including Val176's CG2 sitting a few angstroms away from Lys195's NZ.

Continuing down the list, Lys216's NZ, Arg215, Arg224's guanidinium atoms, and Arg231's whole side chain all look isolated from other residues based on the coordinates. I'm now checking Arg232's side chain against nearby His230 to see if there's a potential contact there.

Checking Glu219, Glu226, Glu237, and Glu245 against nearby residues for possible salt bridges or close contacts, I'm not finding clear matches within bonding distance for any of them so far — the closest candidates like Thr235, Thr249, and Ala250 are still several angstroms away.

I continue checking Glu269, finding it isolated from Asn270. Moving to glutamines, I check Gln138 against Ser127 (too far), Gln159 against Ser183 (borderline at 3.5Å for NE2), and I'm now examining Gln182's proximity to Val277.

I find Gln182 NE2 sits about 3.3Å from Val277 CG1, which is acceptable. Checking Gln196, its OE1 is 4.8Å from Met252 SD, so that's fine too.

For Gln203, I notice NE2 is roughly 3.3-3.4Å from Lys195 NZ, which is a mild concern since both are nitrogen atoms. I'm moving on to check Gln204's geometry now.

Gln210, Gln217, and Gln265 all check out as isolated with no close contacts.

Now I'm working through the Met residues, starting with Met145 — its SD is about 3.6Å from His188 CB, and I'm continuing to check distances to His188 CG as well.

Met149 also looks isolated, with no nearby residues within range after checking Lys153, Ser154, and Thr157.

Now I'm checking Met180's proximity to Val277, Leu257, Ile275, Thr156, and Leu158, none of which seem close enough yet.

Leu191 CD2 to SD gives a distance around 3.9, acceptable.

For Met181, checking against Met145's SD and CE gives distances around 4.2-4.9, borderline but possible. Leu148 CD2 also seems too far.

For Met190, I'm checking Val179, Ile247, Ile243, and Met181, but none seem close enough — still working through Leu191 and Phe189 as neighbors.

For Met252, Ile251's CG2 lands close to SD at around 3.9.

Met281 looks isolated with no nearby contacts.

Now I'm moving to tryptophan residues — Trp137, Trp178, Trp236 — checking their ring atoms against nearby glycine, valine, serine, and tyrosine residues, with Gly139 backbone nitrogen coming in around 3.8 from Trp137's CZ2, and Cys128's sulfur too far to matter. Moving on to map out Trp178's ring geometry next.

For Trp178, I'm checking distances to Ile170, Val176, Ala167, and Leu193 — Ile170's CG2 sits close to CH2 at about 3.9, Val176's CG1 is near CZ2 around 3.7, Ala167's CB is close to NE1 at roughly 3.8, and Leu193's CD2 comes within about 3.7 of CE3.

Now I'm mapping out the ring coordinates for Trp236 to check its nearby contacts next.

Checking Tyr223's OH position against other nearby residues, but nothing lines up closely enough. Moving on to scan the histidine residues (147, 150, 152, 188, 230, 244) for proximity, starting with His150 which looks isolated, then checking His188's position.

For His188, I find its ND1 sits about 2.8 Å from Ser183's OG, close enough to form a reasonable hydrogen bond. His230 also appears isolated with no close contacts. For His244, I'm checking distances to Tyr126's CE1 and OH atoms, but they seem too far apart to be significant.

Checking His152, I find its NE2 sits roughly 2.1 Å from the zinc ion, indicating it's also coordinating the metal alongside Cys128, Cys135, and His147. This gives a four-coordinate zinc site typical of a zinc finger motif, with Cys130 potentially left as a free thiol or involved in a disulfide bond worth checking against Cys256.

Now I'm scanning Phe165's ring atoms against nearby hydrophobic residues (Val192, Leu193, Val179, Ile275, Leu257, Ala207, Met180) to see if any fall within packing distance of its aromatic ring.

For Phe185, I'm checking the ring positions against Ser280 and Ile279, measuring distances from CZ to their side-chain atoms to spot any close contacts.

I'm checking Phe187's ring atoms against nearby residues, comparing distances to Asn220, Gln217, and Leu211 to find close contacts.

I'm checking distances from Phe205's ring atoms to nearby residues like Lys195, Thr261, and Ala264, measuring if any fall within contact range.

Now checking Pro260, Leu227, Gln203, and Ile263 side chains against the target atom, then moving on to map out Phe206's backbone and ring coordinates for the same comparison.

I'm scanning nearby residues like Ile251, Met252, Lys195, Gln196, and Val258 to see if any of their side chain atoms fall close enough to be relevant contacts.

Now checking Phe221's ring atoms against Phe185, Phe187, Met281, Ser183, and Leu211, none seem close enough—distances are running 3.5-4Å or more.

I'm moving on to examine Phe259's CB and CG coordinates next.

Checking Phe267's coordinates against nearby residues to see which side chains fall within contact distance, testing Leu227, Ile263, and Leu266 but none land close enough.

Now I'm examining Tyr126's ring positions against Leu141's atoms and Ile243, computing distances but still not finding a clear clash — I'm starting to think the overlap might instead involve backbone atoms rather than side chains.

Maybe the clash isn't between these residues at all — perhaps it involves the Zn coordination itself, though those bond distances (2.05-2.29 Å) look normal, and Cys130 SG to Zn at 4.8 Å seems fine too. I should reconsider whether I mis-estimated a CA position and missed a pair, so I'll try a more systematic atom-level search.

I'm going to scan for atoms with similar coordinates across all residue pairs, sorting them into spatial slabs to narrow down candidates, since checking all 1159 atoms exhaustively is heavy but focusing on interior packing regions where clashes typically occur makes sense — though surface contacts are possible too. The severest clash the question describes is likely something like a 2.4 Å carbon-carbon contact, and my scan is turning up minimum non-bonded distances to pin that down.

I'm checking specific residue pairs for close backbone or sidechain contacts: several turn out to be hydrogen bonds (like Asp162-Thr278 and His188-Ser183), so I need to look elsewhere, including backbone O-N distances across tight turns and chain breaks, but those checks keep coming back far apart.

Since manual pairwise checks aren't finding it, I'm switching to a systematic grid-based approach, binning each residue's CA coordinates into 8 Å cells so I can spot nearby residues that are close in space but far apart in sequence.

Still computing coordinate grid positions...

Still computing grid coordinates...

Still computing coordinates and grid cell assignments for each point...

Computing more coordinate mappings...

Still listing coordinate data...

Still computing coordinates and cell indices...

Still listing coordinates...

Now I'm scanning for residue pairs that share the same or adjacent grid cells but are far apart in sequence, checking cells I haven't covered yet, starting with cell (-1,-1,-1).

Checking Pro129 against Ile243 distances, they're too far apart, so I'm shifting to check neighboring lattice cells for closer contacts.

Now I'm scanning residues 178, 179, 180, 192 near cell (0,-1,-1), plus 165 from the adjacent cell, but the distances between Trp178 and 192 come out too large again. Moving on to check cell (0,-2,-1) with residues 154, 155, 156.

Checking residue 156's threonine side chain against Met180's CB, but the distance is still too far for contact. I'm now looking at cells (-1,-2,-1) and (-1,-3,-1), checking His152 and Met149's side chains, but again the separation is too large. Moving on to cell (-1,-1,0) covering residues 181, 182, 188, 189, and 191.

Checking Phe189's CB against Val209's CG2, the gap is around 4 angstroms but overall distance is still too far, and similarly for 191 vs 209 and 182 vs 191 — none of these are close enough. In cell (-1,0,-1) with residue 247, I'm comparing Ile247's CD1 against Ile251's CB, but that pairing doesn't work out either. Now shifting to cell (-1,1,-1) with residues 250, 251, 253, and 255.

I'm checking Ala250's CB against Asn253's side chain atoms, finding the ND2 nitrogen is about 5.2 angstroms away in the y-direction alone — too far. Then I'm looking at Asp255 near Trp236, comparing various side chain atoms like OD1 and OD2 against the tryptophan's ring carbons CZ2 and CH2, getting distances around 3.6-4.4 angstroms, which is promising but I need to verify more carefully.
